inventory.anchor: PeerConnectionImpl::Initialize, where the proxy config of the PeerConnection is handed to its transport handler
inventory.notes: GetProxyConfig returns no config for a window that was torn down (a detached iframe, a closed popup: no BrowserChild, and LoadInfo::Create refuses a document without ClientInfo), and a PeerConnection with no config has plain sockets and a resolver in the default context. StealthProxyConfigOf (StealthIceResolverContext.cpp) keeps upstream's config when there is one and otherwise builds it from the principal of the window, so the sockets stay behind the proxy of the page's context; with no principal the proxy is forced.

inventory.anchor: WebrtcTCPSocket::DoProxyConfigLookup and OpenWithHttpProxy (the channel of the proxy lookup and of the HTTP tunnel)
inventory.notes: The channel of the proxy lookup of a PeerConnection's TCP socket (TURN over TCP) is made by StealthNewChannelOfLoadInfo, with the load info of the document: the proxy filters answer for the context of the page, not for the system principal's. The HTTP tunnel's own channel is made by the same function (the code it had is gone from here). In OpenWithoutHttpProxy one call of StealthTcpNameContext (network/doh, body in StealthIceResolverContext.cpp) gives the socket transport the origin attributes of the PeerConnection right after CreateTransport, so a TURN name over TCP is resolved in the context of the page.

inventory.anchor: include of nr_stealth_proxy_udp.h; NrSocket::create (UDP: the proxy layer); NrSocketBase::CreateSocket (the config to NrSocket; no UDP socket of a PeerConnection in a content process)
inventory.notes: The rule of the UDP of a PeerConnection, made where its socket is born: no proxy = a plain socket, SOCKS5 = the SOCKS5 UDP layer, a proxy without UDP = a socket whose datagrams go nowhere. In a content process the UDP sockets of a PeerConnection are refused (they would go out direct). Also (feature webrtc-declared-network, fingerprint/webrtc/declared-network): a host UDP socket of a declared address binds the wildcard of its family on the port of its connection and reports the declared address with that port; a datagram between two sockets of this process goes on the kernel's loopback while each end sees the other's declared address (StealthOwnPorts).
